record.paper_title: Operations Research challenges in forestry: 33 open problems
record.original_question: Wildlife reserve decisions are made sequentially over time, and the planner must account for uncertain site availability, habitat quality, budgets, land development, and price feedbacks caused by earlier reserve choices. The open question is how to formulate and solve dynamic reserve selection and reserve design problems that capture those effects at realistic scales.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 17 How can we develop effective formulations and solution methods for dynamic reserve selection and design problems with land price feedbacks and uncertainty about site availability, quality and budget?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a wildlife reserve planning setting in which a conservation agency selects parcels of land to acquire and protect over a finite sequence of decision epochs t = 1, 2, ..., T. At each epoch the planner observes a state describing: (i) the set of parcels currently available for purchase, (ii) the habitat quality of each parcel (which may evolve stochastically), (iii) the remaining capital budget (which may itself be random across epochs), (iv) the state of land development on non-reserved parcels, and (v) prevailing parcel prices, which respond endogenously to the planner's prior acquisition decisions (a land-price feedback in which earlier protections raise or lower prices of remaining parcels through amenity premia and equilibrium adjustments). The planner chooses, at each epoch, a subset of currently available parcels to acquire, subject to the current budget, in order to maximize an objective measuring the long-run ecological value of the assembled reserve system (for example, expected total habitat or species representation, possibly with spatial contiguity or compactness requirements).

Develop a mathematical formulation of this sequential stochastic reserve selection and reserve design problem that simultaneously incorporates:
(a) uncertainty about future site availability,
(b) uncertainty about habitat quality,
(c) uncertainty about future budgets,
(d) endogenous land development on unprotected parcels, and
(e) feedback of past reserve decisions on future parcel prices,
together with solution methods (exact or approximate, with provable guarantees or empirically validated performance) capable of handling instances of realistic size, i.e. thousands of candidate parcels and multiple planning periods.
artifact.status_search_result: Several components of this problem have been addressed in the literature. Tóth, Haight, and Rogers (Operations Research, 2011) introduced a dynamic reserve selection model with land-price feedbacks, solved via stochastic dynamic programming and capable of accounting for budget, development, and price uncertainty. Scenario optimization models (e.g., Snyder et al.) and heuristics for large dynamic minimum-set reserve design problems have also appeared. However, no single formulation/solution method has been demonstrated to simultaneously handle all listed uncertainties (availability, quality, budget) together with land-price feedbacks at the realistic scales targeted by the open problem, so the full question remains only partially resolved.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic Reserve Selection: Optimal Land Retention with Land-Price Feedbacks
status_evidence.snippet: Model captures economic theory of competitive land markets in a dynamic framework, with parcel-level recommendations and thousands of potential site selection decisions over several planning periods.
status_evidence.claim: A dynamic reserve selection model addressing land-price feedbacks has been formulated and solved.

status_evidence.title: Dynamic minimum set problem for reserve design: Heuristic solutions for large problems
status_evidence.snippet: Heuristic solutions for large dynamic reserve design problems.
status_evidence.claim: Heuristic methods have been developed for large-scale dynamic reserve design instances.

status_evidence.title: A Scenario Optimization Model for Dynamic Reserve Site Selection
status_evidence.snippet: Scenario-based optimization for dynamic reserve site selection under uncertainty.
status_evidence.claim: Stochastic scenario formulations exist for dynamic reserve site selection.
